title: Multitask linear bandits with unit-ball actions and unit-norm parameters
summary: Multiple linear bandit tasks share an unknown low-dimensional representation. All task actions must be submitted together before the batch of scalar rewards is revealed. Performance is the sum of cumulative pseudo-regret across tasks. Each task has the unit ball as its action set and a unit-norm parameter.

model.instance: There are $M$ parallel tasks, each interacting for $T$ rounds with one action per task per round. The parameter matrix and shared representation satisfy $$\Theta=[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_M],\quad \operatorname{rank}(\Theta)=r,\quad \theta_m=Bw_m,\quad B^{\mathsf T}B=I_r,\quad \|\theta_m\|_2=1.$$. Each task has the fixed action set $\mathcal A_m=B_2^d(1)$. This profile imposes no task-diversity assumption; applicability of the separately listed representation-based upper bound remains pending.

operations.query_signature: Submit all $M$ actions simultaneously and receive all rewards together, with no within-batch sequential feedback. $$Y_{t,m}=\langle x_{t,m},\theta_m\rangle+\eta_{t,m}.$$ The variables $\eta_{t,m}$ are i.i.d. $\mathcal N(0,1)$ across tasks and rounds. Centralized causal policies are allowed. Inputs $d,r,M,T$ are public; the shared basis $B$ and coefficient matrix $W=[w_1,\ldots,w_M]$ are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.
